name: WY at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+23 partisan lean makes the seat effectively unwinnable for Democrats
Chuck Gray holds a roughly 90-to-1 fundraising advantage over Lisa Kinney, plus $1.6M in outside support
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 98 percent
Open seat after Hageman's retirement does not alter the partisan math
model.rationale: The district's 23-point Republican lean, Gray's overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing a GOP victory at 98 percent all point to a safe Republican hold, and nothing in the evidence suggests the open seat changes that.
model.watch: Only an unforeseen development affecting the Republican nominee or a collapse in GOP turnout could bring this margin meaningfully closer.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Harriet Hageman (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Wyoming's at-large House seat is among the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 23 points toward the GOP. With incumbent Harriet Hageman leaving to run for Senate, Republican Chuck Gray enters the general election as a heavy favorite. He has raised about $1.6 million and drawn a similar amount in outside support, while Democrat Lisa Kinney has reported under $20,000 in receipts and roughly $2,000 on hand. Prediction markets price a Republican victory near 98 percent.

The open-seat dynamic does little to change the underlying math, since the Republican primary effectively decided this race. Barring an unexpected late development, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin consistent with the district's fundamentals.
